identity.name: Open Design
identity.one_liner: Local-first open-source design agent for prototypes, decks, dashboards, images, video, and agent-driven design systems.
identity.short_description: Open Design is a local-first, open-source design agent and desktop studio from nexu-io. It turns coding agents and model routers into a design workflow for web, desktop, mobile prototypes, live dashboards, slide decks, images, videos, and reusable design systems.

positioning.why_it_matters: Open Design matters because it moves AI design work out of a closed chat surface and into an inspectable, local-first workflow. Builders can connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Qwen, Copilot, Hermes, Kimi, and other CLIs, then generate artifacts that can be previewed, exported, and handed back to engineering.
best_for: Developers and designers who want an open-source Claude Design alternative
Teams prototyping web apps, dashboards, mobile flows, decks, and branded artifacts with AI agents
Agent builders who want design skills, design systems, plugins, MCP integration, and local-first artifact generation
not_for: Teams that need a mature visual canvas replacement for every Figma collaboration workflow today
Non-technical users who do not want to manage local apps, agent CLIs, model accounts, or self-hosted services
Production teams that cannot tolerate early-stage issues around model behavior, CPU usage, onboarding, or fast-moving releases

core_strengths.title: Agent-native design workflow
core_strengths.description: Open Design connects coding agents, model routers, skills, design systems, and previews into one studio for generating artifacts.

core_strengths.description: The project targets prototypes, dashboards, decks, images, videos, HyperFrames, HTML, PDF, PPTX, MP4, and ZIP exports.

command_line.label: Run Open Design in dev mode
command_line.command: git clone https://github.com/nexu-io/open-design.git && cd open-design && corepack enable && pnpm install && pnpm tools-dev run web
command_line.description: The official quickstart requires Node 24 and pnpm through Corepack for the local development path.

command_line.label: Install the MCP server for Codex
command_line.description: The README documents one-line MCP install commands for supported coding agents, including Codex.

command_line.label: Run the Docker path
command_line.command: cd deploy && cp .env.example .env && docker compose up -d
command_line.description: Use the Docker path if you want a containerized Open Design instance without a full local Node setup.

seo_article.intro: Open Design is a local-first open-source AI design agent for teams that want a Claude Design alternative they can inspect, run, and connect to their own coding agents.
seo_article.what_it_is: Open Design combines a desktop/web studio, design skills, brand-grade design systems, plugins, MCP tooling, sandboxed preview, and export paths for HTML, PDF, PPTX, MP4, and ZIP artifacts. The public repository describes support for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, OpenClaw, Copilot, Qwen, Hermes, Kimi, and other agent CLIs.
seo_article.why_it_matters: The product is important because design agents are becoming part of the software delivery loop. Instead of treating design as a closed prompt UI, Open Design exposes the workflow as files, skills, templates, plugins, agent adapters, previews, and exports.
seo_article.how_it_works: A typical Open Design workflow starts with a skill, a design system, and a prompt. The selected agent streams an artifact into the studio, Open Design previews it in a sandbox, and the user can save or export the result. Version 0.9.0 also emphasizes Open Design AMR, an official model router intended to reduce first-run setup.

alternatives.summary: Figma still owns the collaborative canvas. Open Design is a better fit when the job is agent-generated artifacts, prototypes, decks, and design-system experiments.

faq.question: Is Open Design open source?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub repository is published under Apache-2.0 as of the June 3, 2026 verification for this profile.

faq.question: Is Open Design a Figma replacement?
faq.answer: Not for every workflow. It is better described as an open-source design agent and artifact generator, while Figma remains the mature collaborative visual canvas.

faq.question: What community feedback should teams watch?
faq.answer: GitHub issues show fast iteration and early-stage bugs, including AMR instruction hallucination, macOS CPU usage, conversation startup, billing/invoice, and model/attachment problems. Public Reddit/X feedback was limited in searchable results at verification time, so GitHub remains the strongest visible feedback channel.
